text:
Dallas arrives as the better team on paper. At five on five the Stars have taken 50% of the expected goals in their games, while Chicago sits at 40%. The gap is on defense: DAL allows 2.65 expected goals per 60 against 3.55 for CHI, and both teams generate 2.69 at the other end. The model projects 3.15 expected goals for DAL tonight and 2.66 for CHI. On special teams, DAL's power play produces 0.69 expected goals a game to CHI's 0.40, though DAL takes 4.0 penalties a game, which keeps handing out chances. CHI is on the second night of a seven-game home stand's early stretch, with one day of rest to Dallas's two.

In net, projected starter Jake Oettinger (DAL) has a .944 save percentage and +6.5 goals saved above expected this season, after +2.15 last year. Projected starter Spencer Knight (CHI) sits at .890 and -0.08 this season, though he was +11.11 last season, so the gap may narrow. Recent form is close: DAL is 3-1-1 in its last five with 51% of the expected goals, CHI is 3-2-0 with 48%.

Jason Robertson has a 38% chance to score and Mikko Rantanen a 71% chance at a point, both on the top power play. Wyatt Johnston (35% to score) is day-to-day and could return. For Chicago, Connor Bedard is the one to watch at 32% to score, and Bowen Byram could return from the out list.
